title: Define and Detect High-Quality Listings
prompt:
Airbnb wants to improve guest experience by identifying high-quality listings. How would you define listing quality and design an ML system to identify it?

The reported question gives no prescribed metric, label, or model; the following is practice scaffolding. First choose the action this signal would support, such as host guidance, review, a badge, or ranking. Define the decision unit, prediction time, output, and eligible population for each outcome. Explain candidate labels, data and point-in-time features, a baseline and model, serving and refresh behavior, and validation. Distinguish predictive accuracy from the effect of the action in an online test. Address missing feedback, new listings, market differences, and host safeguards. State assumptions where the report is silent.

response.placeholder: Begin with a time-bound, multi-objective definition of quality; do not collapse every candidate signal into an unexamined label.
response.reference_answer:
## Assumptions and decision

The report asks how to identify quality listings to improve the guest experience; it does not specify labels or a scoring formula. For this proposed design, estimate quality before a listing is shown and tie the score to a reviewable action, such as extra verification or guidance. Separate guest stay experience from whether a booking is fulfilled, and choose outcome windows for each. Retention, reviews, cancellations, disputes, refunds, and NPS are possible practice signals to evaluate, not source-reported requirements or interchangeable labels.

## Labels and features

Define eligible populations before calculating rates. Measure fulfillment failures among confirmed reservations, attributing host-caused and guest-caused cancellations separately. Measure stay issues among started stays, including early departures; a reservation that never starts has no stay-issue label. Assign refunds and disputes to the relevant fulfillment or stay issue according to their timing and cause rather than treating every refund as a booking-stage failure. Record missing feedback and label delay rather than treating them as positive outcomes. Freeze all input features at the pre-display decision time; later reviews, bookings, and support actions are outcomes, not inputs. Separate listing attributes from market and request context. Start with transparent component baselines before considering calibrated multi-task models or permitted text and image features.

## Validation and use

Use time-based and market-held-out evaluation, then inspect calibration and error by listing age, geography, availability, and outcome completeness. Compare any decision rule with a simple baseline and test the proposed intervention against a control: predictive accuracy alone does not establish an improvement in guest experience. Avoid automatically penalizing a new listing for lacking history.

## Serving and monitoring

Serve the score with its uncertainty and a fallback for missing data. Monitor label delay, missingness, score drift, calibration, action rates, and downstream guest, host, and trust outcomes. Offer a review path for consequential host actions, audit relevant slices, and roll back an intervention when its guardrails worsen.
